page: Amazon Web Services c8id.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, translating to 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2202.0 and top-tier text processing capabilities at 2823.0. Single-threaded operations perform well, as evidenced by a gzip compression rate of 34.39 GB/sec and a bzip3 decompression rate of 14.52 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound workloads show relative weaknesses. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark memory score fall into the bottom 25% tier. LLM inference speeds are moderate for small models, but drop to a poor rating of 4.81 tokens/sec for text generation on medium 7B models.

The c8id.xlarge offers a high-frequency CPU and fast DDR5 memory, making it highly efficient for single-threaded tasks and text processing. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides low-latency disk access, which benefits database operations and temporary file processing. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core and weaker multi-core scaling present clear tradeoffs for memory-intensive or highly parallelized applications. This instance is best suited for single-threaded compute tasks, lightweight web serving, text processing pipelines, and workloads requiring fast local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores) running at 3.9 GHz. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz and a 237 GB NVMe SSD local instance store. Benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, particularly in text processing and single-threaded compression, alongside average performance in database operations and static web serving. However, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth represent notable tradeoffs, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark memory scores falling into the lower percentiles. Lacking a GPU, this instance is not designed for heavy AI generation, but its high clock speed and fast local storage make it highly suitable for single-threaded compute tasks, text processing, and lightweight database workloads.
